explanation:
**What the grids are made of.** Each grid is a black background with small single-colour shapes on it. Some shapes are colour 1 and the rest have "real" colours (6, 7, 8, 9, 3, …). In every pair the only cells that change are colour-1 cells. Each colour-1 shape is recoloured as a whole, and colour 1 is gone from every output.

**Which colour does a 1-shape get?** I compared each 1-shape with the coloured shapes in the same grid:

- **Pair 1:**
  - The 1-shape `111/101` gets colour 6. The 6-object is exactly `111/101`.
  - The L-shape `10/11` gets colour 7. The 7-object is `10/11`.
  - The shape `11/01` gets colour 9. The 9-object is `11/01`.
- **Pair 2:** the 1-plus becomes 8, because the 8-object is the same plus.
- **Pair 3:**
  - `010/111/001` becomes 7, the identical 7-shape.
  - `01/11/01` becomes 9.
  - The bar `010/111` becomes 3.
  - The vertical domino becomes 6.

So the rule is: **every colour-1 object takes the colour of the coloured object with exactly the same shape.** The match is on the cropped binary mask, with no rotation needed. In every case there is exactly one such partner.

**Test input.** Each 1-shape has a unique exact partner:

| 1-shape | Partner | New colour |
|---|---|---|
| `011/111/010` (top right) | 8-object at the top | 8 |
| plus (centre) | 6-plus | 6 |
| `010/111` (top left) | 2-object | 2 |
| `01/11/01` | 4-object | 4 |
| vertical domino | 8-domino in the corner | 8 |

**Construction stages.** I start from a copy of the input. I recolour one 1-object at a time and emit after each recolouring. A shape with no partner would be left unchanged. Then I emit and return the final canvas.
